title: Erdős Problem #309: The Axiom-Free Upper Bound F(N) ≤ log N + 2
description: The elementary, fully machine-checked upper-bound half of Erdős #309: the number F(N) of integers representable as sums of distinct unit fractions with denominators from {1,...,N} satisfies F(N) ≤ log N + 2. Self-contained and 0-axiom; bridges the custom harmonic number to Mathlib's `harmonic` to invoke `harmonic_le_one_add_log`.

overview.historicalContext:
**The upper half of a solved Erdős problem.**

Erdős #309 asks how many integers F(N) can be written as a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators from {1,…,N}, and in particular whether F(N) = o(log N). The answer is NO: F(N) = log N + γ + O((log log N)²/log N), so F(N) = Θ(log N) (Yokota 1997/2002, Croot 1999).

The lower direction is deep (Yokota's estimate, axiomatized in the parent entry). The **upper** direction is elementary and is what every source calls the "trivial upper bound": any representable integer k is at most the full harmonic sum H_N = 1 + 1/2 + ⋯ + 1/N, so there are at most ⌊H_N⌋ + 1 ≤ log N + 2 of them. This entry makes that elementary half fully machine-checked and axiom-free, connecting the formalization's custom harmonic number to Mathlib's `harmonic` so that Mathlib's `harmonic_le_one_add_log` (H_N ≤ 1 + log N) can be applied directly.
overview.problemStatement:
**Upper bound (this entry).** For all N, the count F(N) of representable integers satisfies
$$F(N) \le \log N + 2,$$
and for N ≥ 1, $2 \le F(N) \le \log N + 2$. The matching log-order lower bound (Yokota) is the deep direction and is not reproved here.
overview.text: Axiom-free proof of the trivial upper bound F(N) ≤ log N + 2 for Erdős #309, via a bridge from the custom harmonic number to Mathlib's `harmonic`.
overview.proofStrategy:
**Strategy**

1. **Bridge to Mathlib.** Show denominatorRange N = Icc 1 N and that on it unitFraction d = (d:ℚ)⁻¹, so harmonicNumber N equals Mathlib's `harmonic N` (`harmonic_eq_sum_Icc`).
2. **Confine the representable set.** Every representable k has (k:ℚ) ≤ H_N (subset sum of nonnegative unit fractions), hence k ≤ ⌊H_N⌋ by `Nat.le_floor`. So the filtered finset is contained in range(⌊H_N⌋ + 1), giving F(N) ≤ ⌊H_N⌋ + 1.
3. **Apply the analytic bound.** ⌊H_N⌋ ≤ H_N = harmonic N ≤ 1 + log N (`harmonic_le_one_add_log`), so F(N) ≤ (1 + log N) + 1 = log N + 2.
4. **Trivial lower bound.** 0 and 1 are both representable for N ≥ 1, so F(N) ≥ 2.
keyInsights: The 'trivial upper bound' cited in the literature is exactly F(N) ≤ ⌊H_N⌋ + 1, and is fully elementary.
The crux of formalizing it is the bridge harmonicNumber = Mathlib's `harmonic`, after which `harmonic_le_one_add_log` does the analytic work.
Representable integers are confined to {0,1,…,⌊H_N⌋}: a cardinality argument, not an asymptotic one.
The hard Θ(log N) content of Erdős #309 is entirely in the lower bound; the upper bound carries no axioms.

sections.title: Header: The Axiom-Free Upper Bound F(N) ≤ log N + 2
sections.summary: Module docstring: states Erdős Problem #309 (does F(N), the count of integers expressible as a sum of distinct unit fractions with denominators ≤ N, satisfy F(N) = o(log N)?), reports the known answer F(N) = Θ(log N) (Yokota, Croot), notes the parent file no longer builds under current Mathlib, and lists this self-contained file's four zero-axiom results culminating in the elementary bound F(N) ≤ log N + 2.
sections.mathContext: $F(N) \le \lfloor H_N \rfloor + 1 \le \log N + 2$ via Mathlib's `harmonic_le_one_add_log`, where $H_N$ is the $N$-th harmonic number; this is the easy upper half of Erdős #309, the deep matching lower bound (Yokota) is not reproved here.

sections.title: Self-Contained Definitions
sections.summary: A self-contained mirror of the parent file's definitions (the parent no longer builds against Mathlib 4.26.0). unitFraction n = 1/n (0 at n = 0); sumUnitFractions sums over a finite denominator set; denominatorRange N = range(N+1) \ {0} = {1,…,N}; harmonicNumber N = sumUnitFractions (denominatorRange N); IsRepresentable N k means k = ∑_{d ∈ S} 1/d for some S ⊆ {1,…,N}; countRepresentable N = F(N) is the number of representable integers in {0,…,N}.
sections.mathContext: $H_N=\sum_{d=1}^N 1/d$; $k$ representable iff $k=\sum_{d\in S}1/d$ for some $S\subseteq\{1,\dots,N\}$; $F(N)=|\{k\le N:\ k\text{ representable}\}|$.

sections.title: Basic Facts and the Subset-Sum Bound
sections.summary: Membership in denominatorRange (mem_denominatorRange), nonnegativity of unit fractions and the harmonic number, and representability of 0 (empty set) and 1 (the singleton {1}, for N ≥ 1). The key inequality is max_representable_le_harmonic: every representable k satisfies (k:ℚ) ≤ H_N, because its representing set S ⊆ {1,…,N} and all unit fractions are nonnegative, so its subset sum is at most the full sum (Finset.sum_le_sum_of_subset_of_nonneg).
sections.mathContext: $k$ representable $\Rightarrow (k:\mathbb{Q})\le H_N$ (subset sum of nonnegative unit fractions); $0,1$ representable for $N\ge 1$.

sections.title: The Bridge to Mathlib's harmonic
sections.summary: harmonicNumber_eq_harmonic shows the file's custom harmonicNumber N equals Mathlib's harmonic N. Using harmonic_eq_sum_Icc (H_N = ∑_{d ∈ Icc 1 N} 1/d), the proof identifies denominatorRange N = Finset.Icc 1 N and checks unitFraction d = 1/d on that set. This bridge is what unlocks Mathlib's analytic estimate harmonic_le_one_add_log.

sections.title: The Axiom-Free Upper Bound F(N) ≤ log N + 2
sections.summary: countRepresentable_le_floor_harmonic confines the representable integers to {0,…,⌊H_N⌋} (via Nat.le_floor on the subset-sum bound), giving F(N) ≤ ⌊H_N⌋ + 1 by a cardinality comparison. countRepresentable_le_log_add_two — the headline result — chains F(N) ≤ ⌊H_N⌋ + 1 ≤ H_N + 1 with the bridge and Mathlib's harmonic_le_one_add_log (H_N ≤ 1 + log N) to conclude F(N) ≤ log N + 2, fully machine-checked and axiom-free.

sections.title: The Trivial Lower Bound and the Bracket
sections.summary: two_le_countRepresentable: since 0 and 1 are both representable for N ≥ 1, the filtered finset contains {0,1}, so F(N) ≥ 2. countRepresentable_bracket packages 2 ≤ F(N) ≤ log N + 2 for N ≥ 1. The upper bound is sharp up to the additive constant; the matching log-order lower bound F(N) ≥ log N − O(log log N) is the deep Yokota direction (axiomatized in the parent) and is NOT reproved here.
sections.mathContext: $2\le F(N)\le\log N+2$ for $N\ge 1$; lower bound from $0,1$ representable, upper bound from the harmonic estimate.

conclusion.summary: Working self-containedly (the parent Erdos309Problem.lean no longer builds against Mathlib 4.26.0), this file proves the elementary upper-bound half of Erdős #309: the count F(N) of integers representable as sums of distinct unit fractions with denominators in {1,…,N} satisfies F(N) ≤ log N + 2, with the matching trivial lower bound F(N) ≥ 2 for N ≥ 1. The argument confines the representable integers to {0,…,⌊H_N⌋} by a subset-sum bound, bridges the file's harmonic number to Mathlib's harmonic, and applies harmonic_le_one_add_log. 182 lines, 11 theorems, 6 definitions, 0 axioms, 0 sorries (verified with only propext, Classical.choice, Quot.sound; the single decide is kernel-level, not native_decide).
conclusion.implications: Erdős #309 is solved (F(N) = log N + γ + O((log log N)²/log N), Yokota/Croot), so F(N) = Θ(log N). The deep content is entirely in the lower bound; the upper bound is what the literature calls 'trivial', and this entry makes it fully machine-checked and axiom-free — an honest record of the easy half, explicitly leaving the Yokota lower bound to the (axiomatized) parent. The contribution is the careful Mathlib bridge harmonicNumber = harmonic, which turns a custom formalization into one that can invoke upstream analytic estimates.
openQuestions: Reprove the deep Yokota lower bound F(N) ≥ log N − O(log log N) axiom-free, replacing the parent's axiom yokota_lower_bound_1997 and completing the F(N) = Θ(log N) result without assumptions.
Sharpen the additive constant: the truth is F(N) = log N + γ + o(1) (γ the Euler–Mascheroni constant); formalize the refined asymptotic, not merely the +2 bound.
